correctness.rationale: For any existing finite projective plane of order q, v=q²+q+1 is odd, and point-line incidence N over F2 satisfies NNᵀ=NᵀN=(q mod 2)I+J and J²=J. Thus F=[[0,N],[Nᵀ,0]] has F⁴=F², and periodic states are exactly im F². Even q gives the 2-dimensional exchange subspace, four periodic states, two fixed and one 2-cycle; rank(F)=2ρ and the square-zero transient factor produce exact entry-time counts 4, 2^(2v-2ρ+2)-4, 2^(2v)-2^(2v-2ρ+2), and size-two zero blocks 2ρ-2. Odd q yields F³=F, recurrent dimension 2v-2, fixed dimension v-1 and precisely 3·2^(2v-2) states entering after one step. The q-even sharpness follows from ρ>1 (distinct nonzero incidence rows); q-odd sharpness from the two-dimensional zero factor. The source explicitly assumes plane existence, not arbitrary q. Independent binary matrix identities for PG(2,2), PG(2,3) and all 16384 states at q=2 reproduce entry counts (4,252,16128). These experiments corroborate, rather than prove, the all-plane assertion.
residual_risks: The even-order counts depend on the plane-specific binary rank ρ; no uniform rank formula for non-Desarguesian planes is claimed.
Finite projective-plane enumeration only checks orders two and three; the universal proof uses incidence axioms.

value.rationale: The complete orbit partition and sharp extinction-entry times are mathematically natural dynamical invariants of a canonical finite-geometric incidence graph. The q-parity phase separation and explicit dependence on the binary incidence rank are useful even when the plane is non-Desarguesian; they distinguish states with immediate cyclic behavior from transient synchronization. This is more than a renamed incidence rank statement.
residual_risks: The proof is short once the classical design identity is known; significance is confined to this exact graph dynamical model and is not a new coding theorem.

limitations: Only existing finite projective planes and synchronous open-neighborhood binary XOR; for even q the rank rho is plane-dependent. Full historical literature coverage is not asserted.
